title: X11: Update and "static"-ify the dissector.
description:
This series of changes updates the X11 dissector and "static"-ifies many of its symbols.

The X11 Mesa update removes two enum values: `TABLE_TOO_LARGE_EXT` and `TEXTURE_INDEX_SIZE_EXT`.  Those were removed from Mesa in https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/merge_requests/14085 , and the discussion there suggests that it is vanishingly unlikely that these values will be seen in the real world -- other than perhaps by the participants in that discussion.  I do not think there is much value in trying to preserve those enumerated values in the dissector; Please let me know if you disagree.

The end result of "static"-ifying the dissector is a reduction in code size by 29 kBytes, because the `int* const` bitfield arrays are being initialized on the stack upon each function entry, and that code is no longer needed once the data structures are present in a read-only data section.  The down side is the gain of 52 kBytes (!) of relocation entries to fix up the references in the relocatable read-only data section, which will be done once (efficiently) by the dynamic linker at link time...

commits_data.title: X11: static-ify the generated dissector.
commits_data.message:
X11: static-ify the generated dissector.

Many of the generated "const" fields can be made static.  For local variables,
this means that the compiler will no longer emit code to allocate the structure
on the stack and initialize it upon each function entry -- 29 kBytes of code in
total gets removed by this change -- which is surely a performance win when
dissecting this protocol.

Interestingly, libwireshark.so ends up growing overall due to the addition of
52 kBytes of relocation entries to patch up references within the relocatable
read-only data section.  Clearly the generated code was more space-efficient
than the relocation entries...
